ForestSearch: Exploratory Subgroup Identification

Source: R/forestsearch_main.R
forestsearch.Rd

Implements advanced statistical methods for exploratory subgroup identification in clinical trials. Provides tools for identifying patient subgroups with differential treatment effects using machine learning approaches including Generalized Random Forests ('GRF'), LASSO regularization, and exhaustive combinatorial search algorithms. Supports survival endpoints (Cox proportional hazards), binary outcomes (log odds ratio, log relative risk, risk difference), continuous outcomes (mean difference), and count / rate outcomes (log incidence rate ratio via Poisson, quasi-Poisson, or negative-binomial GLMs with optional person-time offset). Features bootstrap bias correction using infinitesimal jackknife methods to address selection bias in post-hoc analyses. Designed for clinical researchers conducting exploratory subgroup analyses in randomized controlled trials, particularly for multi-regional clinical trials ('MRCT') requiring regional consistency evaluation. Methods are described in Leon et al. (2024) doi:10.1002/sim.10163 .

Usage

forestsearch(
  df.analysis,
  outcome.name = "tte",
  event.name = "event",
  treat.name = "treat",
  id.name = "id",
  potentialOutcome.name = NULL,
  flag_harm.name = NULL,
  confounders.name = NULL,
  parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = .default_parallel_workers(),
    show_message = TRUE),
  df.predict = NULL,
  df.test = NULL,
  is.RCT = TRUE,
  seedit = 8316951,
  est.scale = "hr",
  use_lasso = FALSE,
  use_grf = FALSE,
  grf_res = NULL,
  grf_cuts = NULL,
  use_dina = FALSE,
  dina_res = NULL,
  dina_cuts = NULL,
  dina_args = list(),
  dina_select_statistic = c("effect", "dina"),
  subgroup_method = c("consistency", "dina", "grf"),
  max_n_confounders = 1000,
  grf_depth = 2,
  grf_selection = c("frontier", "tree"),
  grf_select_statistic = c("effect", "dr"),
  dmin.grf = 0,
  frac.tau = 0.8,
  return_selected_cuts_only = TRUE,
  conf_force = NULL,
  defaultcut_names = NULL,
  cut_type = "default",
  exclude_cuts = NULL,
  replace_med_grf = FALSE,
  cont.cutoff = 4,
  conf.cont_medians = NULL,
  conf.cont_medians_force = NULL,
  conf.cont_jcuts = NULL,
  collapse_cuts = TRUE,
  collapse_cuts_args = list(),
  n.min = 60,
  n.min.frac = 0.1,
  effect.threshold = NULL,
  consistency.threshold = NULL,
  hr.threshold = 1.25,
  hr.consistency = 1,
  sg_focus = "hr",
  selection_rule = "neighborhood",
  effect_neighborhood = 0.1,
  fs.splits = 1000,
  m1.threshold = Inf,
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.9,
  stop_threshold = pconsistency.threshold,
  pconsistency.digits = 2,
  show_candidate_summary = FALSE,
  max_print = 10,
  d0.min = 10,
  d1.min = 10,
  max.minutes = 3,
  minp = 0.025,
  details = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE,
  maxk = 2,
  by.risk = 12,
  plot.sg = FALSE,
  plot.grf = FALSE,
  max_subgroups_search = Inf,
  vi.grf.min = NULL,
  use_twostage = TRUE,
  twostage_args = list(),
  consistency_method = c("resample", "split"),
  outcome_type = c("survival", "binary", "continuous", "count"),
  effect_measure = NULL,
  offset.name = NULL,
  adverse_outcome = NULL,
  overdispersion = c("none", "quasi", "negbin"),
  grf_count_transform = c("log", "identity"),
  tune_grf = FALSE,
  adjust_covariates = NULL,
  ps_method = NULL,
  ps_adjust_method = c("none", "iptw", "dr_gcomp"),
  ps_hat = NULL,
  mr_inference = FALSE,
  mr_inference_args = list()
)

Arguments

df.analysis

Data frame. Analysis dataset with required columns.

outcome.name

Character. Name of time-to-event outcome variable. Default "tte".

event.name

Character. Name of event indicator (1=event, 0=censored). Default "event".

treat.name

Character. Name of treatment variable (1=treatment, 0=control). Default "treat".

id.name

Character. Name of subject ID variable. Default "id".

potentialOutcome.name

Character. Name of potential outcome variable (optional).

flag_harm.name

Character. Name of true harm flag for simulations (optional).

confounders.name

Character vector. Names of candidate subgroup-defining variables.

parallel_args

List. Parallel processing configuration:

plan

Character. One of "multisession" (default; cross-platform, reuses workers across calls), "multicore" (Linux/macOS only, fastest startup but fails in RStudio interactive sessions), "callr" (slower per-call, fully isolated R processes), or "sequential" (no parallelism).

workers

Integer. Number of parallel workers. Default: floor(0.80 * N) where N is the number of physical (non-hyperthreaded) cores, capped to 2 when _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ is set (e.g., during R CMD check). On a 4-core laptop the default is 3 workers; on a 16-core workstation it is 12.

show_message

Logical. Show parallel setup messages.

batch_size

Integer. Number of candidate subgroups dispatched to the workers per batch during consistency evaluation. Default: chosen from the worker count and pool size. This is a performance knob only – it does not affect the selected subgroup. Smaller batches let an early stop take effect sooner (relevant only for sg_focus = "maxeffCons", the one focus that early-stops); larger batches amortise dispatch overhead. Not to be confused with twostage_args$batch.size, which batches splits within Stage 2 of the two-stage consistency algorithm – a different quantity in different units.

To disable parallelism entirely, pass parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential").

df.predict

Data frame. Prediction dataset (optional).

df.test

Data frame. Test dataset (optional).

is.RCT

Logical. Is this a randomized controlled trial? Default TRUE.

seedit

Integer. Random seed. Default 8316951.

est.scale

Character. Estimation scale ("hr" or "rmst"). Default "hr".

use_lasso

Logical. Use LASSO for variable selection. Default FALSE. The default changed from TRUE in an earlier release: with subgroup_method = "consistency" a model-based front end makes the candidate family data-dependent, which multiplier resampling (mr_inference = TRUE) requires be fixed. Set TRUE to restore the prognostic-lasso prefilter used in Leon et al. (2024).

use_grf

Logical. Generate additional candidate cuts from a GRF fit: tree-derived cutpoints are extracted via grf.subg.harm.survival() / grf.subg.harm.glm() (or taken from grf_res / grf_cuts when supplied) and enter the candidate family through get_FSdata alongside the quartile (and any DINA) cuts. This is the only switch that fits a GRF in the forest-search path (the former variable-importance screening, vi.grf.min, is deprecated and inert). Default FALSE. The default changed from TRUE in an earlier release, for the same fixed-candidate-family reason given under use_lasso.

grf_res

GRF results object (optional, for reuse).

grf_cuts

List. Custom GRF cut points (optional).

use_dina

Logical. Generate additional screening-stage candidate cuts from a DINA per-covariate Pareto frontier, fed into get_FSdata alongside the GRF cuts. Default FALSE (opt-in); existing behaviour is unchanged when FALSE.

dina_res

A fitted DINA object (optional, for reuse). When NULL and use_dina = TRUE, a DINA model is fit at the screening stage.

dina_cuts

Character vector of pre-supplied DINA cut expressions (optional). When supplied, the DINA fit / frontier step is skipped and these are used directly.

dina_args

Named list of DINA tuning options, all optional. Recognised keys: family (defaults to the mapping from outcome_type: survival -> cox, binary -> binomial, continuous -> gaussian, count -> poisson), seed (defaults to seedit), and the fit-only keys n_folds, cens_type, cens_params (passed to dina only when set); plus the frontier keys forwarded to dina_frontier: scope (default "wide"), m_diff, n_min (defaults to the n.min of this call), direction, max_per_covariate, max_subgroups, and digits; plus the screening-behavior keys selected_only (default TRUE, matching GRF's return_selected_cuts_only), max_depth (2L default – aligning DINA with maxk = 2 and grf_depth = 2 so the selected cut may be an AND-conjunction of two covariates; set 1L for single-covariate cuts only), and grid_probs (the per-covariate quantile grid for depth-2 pair thresholds; default interior deciles). max_depth / grid_probs are forwarded to dina_subgroup and apply to both the selected-cut screening and subgroup_method = "dina". (The selector statistic formerly accepted here as select_statistic is now the top-level dina_select_statistic argument; a value supplied inside dina_args is deprecated and overridden with a warning.) When selected_only = TRUE (the default), use_dina screening contributes the cut(s) chosen by dina_subgroup – using this call's sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood / n.min / hr.threshold, i.e. the same cut subgroup_method = "dina" would select. Set FALSE to contribute the full frontier candidate set instead.

m_diff is the candidacy floor, on the link scale, and is derived rather than taken from this list. It is the harm floor a candidate must clear to enter the qualifying family that sg_focus then ranks – log(HR) for cox, log(OR) for binomial, log(IRR) for poisson, and the raw mean difference for gaussian. Under subgroup_method = "dina" (and under selected_only = TRUE screening) it is computed as log(hr.threshold) – identity for gaussian – from the resolved effect.threshold, and an m_diff supplied here is ignored. Set the floor with effect.threshold / hr.threshold. The key remains meaningful only where the raw dina_frontier candidate set is used directly.

The same holds for every frontier key, not only m_diff. All seven – scope, m_diff, n_min, direction, max_per_covariate, max_subgroups and digits – are inert under subgroup_method = "dina", which selects with dina_subgroup and never consults a frontier table. Under use_dina = TRUE screening with selected_only = TRUE (the default) a frontier is computed and then discarded in favour of the selected cut, so six of the seven change nothing; only digits still acts, rounding the threshold in the emitted cut expression. The seven keys govern the candidate pool only under selected_only = FALSE, where dina_frontier's cut_expr column is the pool. Supplying any of the seven under subgroup_method = "dina" now raises a single warning() naming every offending key.

Under dina_select_statistic = "effect" the floor still defines the qualifying family on the tau-hat scale while selection re-ranks that family on the refit inferential effect; because multiplier resampling de-biases over the realized selection event, m_diff fixes the family MR de-biases over. See dina_subgroup. Unknown keys raise an error.

dina_select_statistic

Character, one of "effect" (default) or "dina", used only when subgroup_method = "dina". The DINA analogue of grf_select_statistic. "dina" ranks DINA's qualifying family on its native subgroup-mean tau-hat (unchanged legacy behaviour). "effect" re-ranks the same family on the inferential effect measure (Cox HR for survival; the resolved GLM effect otherwise), scored with the same per-candidate estimator multiplier resampling (MR) uses, so the realized selection is the exact event MR de-biases (and MR's native-family restriction follows the effect rather than tau-hat). "effect" is the default because only it ranks on the inferential coefficient; "dina" is rejected under mr_inference = TRUE.

subgroup_method

Character, one of "consistency" (default), "dina", or "grf". "consistency" is the standard ForestSearch pipeline (GRF/LASSO screening then the consistency search). "dina" delegates subgroup selection to dina_subgroup and bypasses GRF, LASSO and the consistency search: a DINA model is fit, a single subgroup is selected using this call's sg_focus / selection_rule / effect_neighborhood / n.min / hr.threshold, and that subgroup is returned as sg.harm. dina_args supplies only the DINA fit tuning in this mode (frontier keys are ignored). "grf" is the GRF analogue: it delegates selection to the GRF subgroup-identification routine (grf.subg.harm.survival for survival, grf.subg.harm.glm for GLM outcomes), again bypassing LASSO, DINA and the consistency search, and returns the policy-tree harm leaf as sg.harm. GRF-selection mode is configured from this call's existing GRF arguments (frac.tau, dmin.grf, grf_depth, is.RCT, seedit, and the GLM extras) – there is no separate argument list – so it uses the same settings GRF screening would. For both "dina" and "grf", the existing bootstrap de-biasing applies unchanged, re-fitting and re-selecting on each replicate. The selected subgroup may be a single covariate or, where the method's depth allows (DINA max_depth = 2; GRF grf_depth >= 2), an AND-conjunction.

max_n_confounders

Deprecated (0.4.0.9000): accepted and ignored with a warning. GRF variable-importance screening of the candidate cut columns was removed so that the candidate family is the cut grid alone unless use_lasso, use_grf or use_dina is TRUE. It capped the importance-ordered column list, which no longer exists. Will be removed in a future release; drop it from the call.

grf_depth

Integer. GRF tree depth. Default 2.

grf_selection

Character, one of "frontier" (default) or "tree", used only when subgroup_method = "grf". "tree" selects via the GRF policy tree. "frontier" selects from the Pareto frontier of the doubly-robust scores (see grf.subg.harm.survival); the frontier rule is taken from sg_focus – "eff", "effMaxSG", "effMinSG", "maxSG" and "minSG" each map to the aligned frontier rule, as in dina_subgroup() – and the relative band from effect_neighborhood. "maxeff" and "maxeffCons" map explicitly to the plain effect-argmax rule ("eff"), the same rule "hr" takes: GRF computes no Pcons, so the Cons qualifier has nothing to bind to. The mapping is exhaustive over the canonical foci and raises an error rather than falling through, so no focus can silently select under a rule the caller did not request. (Earlier versions had no branch for these two and defaulted them to "effMaxSG" silently; pairing them with grf_selection = "frontier" is now well defined.) "frontier" is the default because it enumerates a family that can be ranked on the inferential effect; the policy tree exposes no such family, so "tree" is rejected under mr_inference = TRUE.

grf_select_statistic

Character, one of "effect" (default) or "dr", used only when subgroup_method = "grf" and grf_selection = "frontier". "dr" selects the frontier winner on GRF's native doubly-robust score (legacy behaviour). "effect" re-ranks the same DR-candidate frontier on the inferential effect measure (Cox HR for survival; the resolved GLM effect otherwise), scored with the same per-candidate estimator multiplier resampling (MR) uses, so the realized selection is the exact event MR de-biases (and MR's native-family restriction follows the effect rather than the DR score). "effect" is the default because only it ranks on the inferential coefficient; "dr" is rejected under mr_inference = TRUE. Ignored for grf_selection = "tree" (the policy-tree leaf is the selection, with no enumerated family to rank).

dmin.grf

Numeric. Minimum events for GRF. Default 0.0.

frac.tau

Numeric in (0, 1]. Multiplier on the GRF time horizon passed to grf::causal_survival_forest(). The effective horizon is frac.tau * min(max(Y[treated, event]), max(Y[control, event])), i.e. frac.tau times the smaller of the two arm-specific maximum event times. Values < 1 truncate the horizon inward of that maximum (the conservative choice when events are sparse near the tail). Used by the downstream call to grf.subg.harm.survival. Used only when outcome_type = "survival"; ignored for GLM outcomes (binary, continuous, count). Default 0.8.

return_selected_cuts_only

Logical. If TRUE (default), GRF returns only cuts from the tree depth that identified the selected subgroup meeting dmin.grf. If FALSE returns all cuts from all fitted trees (depths 1 through grf_depth). See grf.subg.harm.survival for details.

conf_force

Character vector of forced cut expressions (optional), e.g. c("er <= 0", "pgr <= 10"). Literal cut locations: unlike the conf.cont_* arguments these do not move with a resample.

defaultcut_names

Character vector. Default cut variable names (optional).

cut_type

Character. Cut strategy: "default" or "median". Default "default". These are the only permitted values – get_FSdata() validates against them and errors otherwise.

exclude_cuts

Character vector. Variables to exclude from cutting (optional).

replace_med_grf

Logical. Replace median with GRF cuts. Default FALSE.

cont.cutoff

Integer. Cutoff for continuous vs categorical. Default 4.

conf.cont_medians

Character vector of continuous confounders to cut at their median (optional). Names, not values – the cut location is the median computed from the supplied data, so it is not fixed by this argument and moves with a resample. To pin a cut location, pass a literal cut expression via conf_force.

conf.cont_medians_force

Character vector of additional continuous confounders to force a median cut on (optional). Names, not values, with the same consequence as conf.cont_medians above.

conf.cont_jcuts

Named integer list (each value >= 1). Per-variable J-quantile cut override for continuous covariates: for an entry X = J, the default cut set for X is replaced by J binary cut points at the (k/(J+1))-th quantiles of X (k = 1, ..., J), defining J+1 non-overlapping intervals. Names must be in confounders.name and must not overlap with defaultcut_names or conf.cont_medians_force. J-cut variables bypass LASSO filtering, matching defaultcut_names semantics. Variables not listed retain default behaviour. Forwarded to get_FSdata via filter_call_args(); see there for full semantics.

collapse_cuts

Logical. If TRUE, collapse near-redundant continuous candidate cuts before the search. Continuous covariates can generate many thresholds that are practically redundant (e.g. "age <= 35.7" and "age <= 35"); when enabled, cuts on the same variable and operator within a per-variable standard-error band are merged to a single rounded-centroid threshold, subject to a membership safety check. Forwarded to get_FSdata; see collapse_redundant_cuts for the algorithm. Default TRUE. Pass collapse_cuts = FALSE to recover the un-coarsened candidate pool used by earlier package versions.

collapse_cuts_args

List of overrides merged onto the defaults list(c = 1.0, tol = 0.05, digits = 0L): band multiplier c (band = c * sd(x)/sqrt(n)), membership safety tolerance tol (fraction of n when < 1, absolute count when >= 1), and representative rounding digits. Ignored when collapse_cuts = FALSE.

n.min

Integer or NULL. Minimum subgroup size. Default 60. Supplying a value (or omitting the argument) uses that fixed floor, as in prior versions. Passing n.min = NULL opts into a sample-size-adaptive floor max(60, ceiling(n.min.frac * N)), where N is the analysis sample size – at least 60, and at least n.min.frac of N. Growing the minimum subgroup size with N curbs false discovery from very small subgroups in large samples. The resolved integer is used everywhere downstream (screening, DINA, GRF, the consistency search, and the bootstrap).

n.min.frac

Numeric in (0, 1). Fraction of the analysis sample size used for the adaptive n.min floor when n.min = NULL. Default 0.10. Ignored when n.min is supplied.

effect.threshold

Numeric or NULL. c1, the screening threshold on a candidate subgroup's own effect, estimated on the full sample. A candidate must clear it to enter the consistency stage. For ratio-scale measures (OR, RR, IRR, HR): on the ratio scale (e.g., 1.5 means OR >= 1.5). For identity-scale measures (RD, IRD, MD): on the identity scale (e.g., 0.07 means RD >= 7 pct points). If NULL (default), falls back to hr.threshold. Distinct from consistency.threshold (c2), which is applied within each split half, and from pconsistency.threshold (p*), which is a proportion rather than an effect. On the consistency path with a ratio estimand (survival HR, binary "OR"), supplying c1 and not c2 derives c2 = 0.80 * c1 on the ratio scale, with a message; see the Threshold vocabulary and resolved defaults section for that rule and for the value this resolves to under each estimand.

consistency.threshold

Numeric or NULL. c2, an effect threshold – not a proportion, and not the consistency rate. It is applied to the subgroup's effect estimated within each split half; a split counts as consistent when both of its halves clear c2. Same scale conventions as effect.threshold. If NULL (default), falls back to hr.consistency. Its companion is pconsistency.threshold (p*), the fraction of splits that must clear c2: this argument sets the bar, that one counts how often the bar is met. Both names contain the word "consistency" and they are different quantities. On the consistency path with a ratio estimand (survival HR, binary "OR") c2 must be less than or equal to c1; c2 > c1 is an error. Left unsupplied there, it is derived as 0.80 * c1 rather than left at its default. See the Threshold vocabulary and resolved defaults section for both rules and for the value this resolves to under each estimand.

hr.threshold

Numeric. Legacy name for effect.threshold – c1, the screening threshold on a candidate subgroup's own effect. Retained for backward compatibility. Default 1.25. When effect.threshold is provided, hr.threshold is ignored; supplying both at disagreeing values is an error. Carries the same c2 derivation as effect.threshold.

hr.consistency

Numeric. Legacy name for consistency.threshold – c2, the per-split effect threshold, not a proportion and not the consistency rate. Retained for backward compatibility. Default 1.0. When consistency.threshold is provided, hr.consistency is ignored; supplying both at disagreeing values is an error. Carries the same c2 <= c1 requirement as consistency.threshold.

sg_focus

Character. Subgroup selection focus – what is selected, not merely how candidates are sorted. Except for "maxeff", every focus selects among qualifiers: candidates whose consistency rate reaches pconsistency.threshold. One of:

"hr" (or "eff", "maxcons")

Pick the qualifier with the highest consistency (Pcons); ties broken by largest effect. This is consistency-primary with effect only as a tiebreak – despite the name, it does not maximise the effect. Use "maxeffCons" for that. "maxcons" is the recommended spelling, since it says what the rule does.

"maxeffCons"

Pick the qualifier with the largest effect; ties broken by fewest cuts (K). The effect maximiser subject to the consistency floor – as against "maxeff", which applies no floor. This is the only focus for which early stopping is sound; see stop_threshold.

"maxSG"

Pick the qualifier with the largest sample size; ties broken by consistency. Not a spelling of "hrMaxSG": it applies no effect band.

"minSG"

Pick the qualifier with the smallest sample size; ties broken by consistency. Not a spelling of "hrMinSG".

"hrMaxSG" (or "effMaxSG")

Among candidates with effect size within effect_neighborhood of the maximum, pick the one with the largest sample size.

"hrMinSG" (or "effMinSG")

Among candidates with effect size within effect_neighborhood of the maximum, pick the one with the smallest sample size.

"maxeff"

The effect maximiser over the enumerated family, with no consistency threshold, effect threshold, early stopping, two-stage screening or candidate-pool truncation. Implements the argmax primitive of Guo and He (2021). Size/event minima (n.min, d0.min, d1.min) still apply as estimability constraints; prevalence and redundancy pruning are relaxed to their most permissive setting (minp -> 0, rmin -> 0) and duplicate removal collapses identical-membership candidates to their fewest-cut representative, so only degenerate or exactly-duplicated candidates are dropped and the argmax is invariant. Because consistency (Pcons) never enters the argmax, it is computed for the SELECTED subgroup only (reported alongside it) rather than for every candidate, avoiding the per-candidate consistency refits. Contrast "maxeffCons", which applies the same argmax but only among candidates clearing pconsistency.threshold, and "hr", which ranks by consistency first and uses effect only as a tiebreaker.

The descriptions above are for subgroup_method = "consistency". There, "maxeffCons" retains both the consistency floor (pconsistency.threshold) and the effect floor, while "maxeff" disables both – the distinction the Cons suffix names.

For subgroup_method = "dina" and "grf", "maxeff" and "maxeffCons" are synonyms, both selecting the effect maximiser over the identifier's qualifiers with the harm floor active. Neither engine has a consistency floor – neither computes Pcons, and no DINA or GRF sort key contains one – so the Cons qualifier has nothing to bind to. The two could in principle have been separated by the effect floor alone; they deliberately are not, because the manuscript keeps the harm threshold in a common form across all three identifiers, and "maxeff" exists for "consistency" as a comparison against the argmax primitive of Guo and He (2021), which has no DINA or GRF counterpart. No floor is disabled by this on any path, and the collapse raises no condition: it is intended behaviour, and a warning would fire on every such run.

Per-engine resolution. Every accepted spelling, and the rule that actually runs for it on each engine:

sg_focusconsistencydina / grf
eff, hr, maxconsconsistency argmax (Pcons-primary, effect breaks ties)effect argmax, order(-eff)
maxeffeffect argmax, no floorseffect argmax, order(-eff)
maxeffConseffect argmax with the consistency flooreffect argmax, order(-eff)
effMaxSG, hrMaxSGlargest N within the effect band, per selection_ruleas documented in dina_subgroup
effMinSG, hrMinSGsmallest N within the effect band, per selection_ruleas documented in dina_subgroup
maxSGlargest N among qualifierslargest N
minSGsmallest N among qualifierssmallest N

The collapse sets, stated explicitly. On "consistency", {eff, hr, maxcons} is one rule, and maxeff and maxeffCons are two further distinct rules. On "dina" and "grf", {eff, hr, maxcons, maxeff, maxeffCons} is one rule – five spellings, one order(-eff).

forestsearch() announces both collapses at run time: when the canonical rule differs from the spelling passed, it emits one message() (suppressed by quiet) naming the rule that will actually run. fs_focus_tag returns the stem tag for each cell of the table above, and is the supported way to label output files by the rule that ran rather than by the spelling requested.

Default "hr". The "eff*" forms are aliases for the "hr*" forms and read more naturally in GLM contexts (continuous MD, binary OR/RR/RD, count IRR) where there is no hazard ratio. Both vocabularies produce identical results; pick whichever fits the outcome type. See sort_subgroups for full sort keys and tiebreakers.

Scope of the band arguments. selection_rule and effect_neighborhood configure the effect band, which only "hrMaxSG" / "hrMinSG" (equivalently "effMaxSG" / "effMinSG") consult. They are inert for every other focus, and supplying selection_rule other than "neighborhood" with a non-band focus is an error rather than a silent no-op.

Choosing between the three effect-oriented rules. "maxeff" answers "what is the most extreme subgroup in this family?"; "maxeffCons" answers "what is the most extreme subgroup that also replicates across splits?"; "hr"/"maxcons" answers "which subgroup replicates most reliably?". They can and do select different subgroups on the same data.

selection_rule

Character. Rule defining the candidate inclusion set for "hrMaxSG" / "hrMinSG". One of "neighborhood" (default; current behaviour), "pareto" (2D Pareto-non-dominated set in (effect, N)), or "both" (intersection of the two). Forwarded to sort_subgroups via filter_call_args(); see there for full semantics. Must be "neighborhood" for other sg_focus values.

effect_neighborhood

Numeric in [0, 1). Relative tolerance for "hrMaxSG" and "hrMinSG" selection. A candidate is in the effect-size neighborhood iff its (natural-scale) effect is at least (1 - effect_neighborhood) * max(effect). Default 0.10 (within 10\ effect_neighborhood = 0 reduces "hrMaxSG"/ "hrMinSG" to a strict max-effect filter (only candidates tied at the maximum qualify). For GLM ratio measures (OR, IRR), the neighborhood test is applied on the natural scale. Ignored when sg_focus is "hr", "maxSG", or "minSG".

fs.splits

Integer. Number of splits for consistency evaluation (or maximum splits when use_twostage = TRUE). Default 1000.

m1.threshold

Numeric. Maximum median survival threshold. Default Inf.

pconsistency.threshold

Numeric. p*, a proportion in [0, 1] – the fraction of random splits that must be consistent, where a split is consistent when both of its halves clear consistency.threshold (c2). It is a rate, not an effect threshold: it never enters an effect comparison, and unlike c1 and c2 it is not remapped per estimand – the same number means the same thing for every outcome_type. Default 0.90. Overridden to 0 under sg_focus = "maxeff" (no consistency filter).

stop_threshold

Numeric in [0, 1] or NULL. Early stopping threshold for consistency evaluation. When a candidate subgroup's consistency probability (Pcons) meets or exceeds this threshold, evaluation stops early – remaining candidates are skipped. Set to NULL to disable early stopping and force evaluation of all candidates up to max_subgroups_search. Defaults to pconsistency.threshold, so it tracks the consistency floor automatically if that is changed.

Applies to sg_focus = "maxeffCons" only. Early stopping halts the scan and then applies the focus's selection key to the resulting prefix, so it is sound only when that key is fully determined by the enumeration order. Pcons is not – it is unknown until a candidate is evaluated – so any focus whose key contains a Pcons term can be beaten by a candidate the scan never reached. "maxeffCons" is the only focus with no such term: its key (-hr, K) is exactly the enumeration order (-HR, K), ties included, so the first qualifying candidate is provably the winner.

For every other focus stop_threshold is reset to NULL, with a warning if it was supplied explicitly:

  • "hr" ("eff", "maxcons") selects on Pcons directly;

  • "maxSG" / "minSG" use Pcons to break ties in subgroup size, which a truncated scan can miss;

  • "hrMaxSG" / "hrMinSG" additionally need the whole pool to compute the effect neighborhood;

  • "maxeff" evaluates only its winner, so early stopping has nothing to skip.

Note: Values > 1.0 are not permitted. To disable early stopping, use stop_threshold = NULL, not a value above 1.

pconsistency.digits

Integer. Number of decimal places to which the consistency proportion is rounded before it is compared with pconsistency.threshold. The rounded value decides admission and is the value the selection sort orders on, so this setting affects which subgroups are admitted, not only what is displayed. At the default of 2, a threshold of p* admits any candidate whose unrounded proportion is at or above the largest 0.01 grid point strictly below p* plus half a step (0.005) – so p* = 0.99 admits from about 0.985. Raising the setting makes admission finer-grained and produces fewer exact ties for the selection rule to break. Under consistency_method = "resample" the proportion is a continuous closed-form quantity, so the rounding is a deliberate coarsening rather than a formatting step. Passed to subgroup.consistency. Default 2.

show_candidate_summary

Logical. If TRUE, prints a post-consistency summary table of all passing candidates with Frontier/InBand/Selected flags. See subgroup.consistency for details. Default FALSE.

max_print

Integer. Maximum number of candidate subgroups to print in the pre- and post-consistency candidate summaries when show_candidate_summary = TRUE. Candidates are printed in sorted order with the selected subgroup first, so max_print = 10 shows the selected subgroup and the next nine, followed by a "... N more not shown" line. Only the per-candidate rows are capped; the banner, header, legend, and summary footer are always printed. Default 10 (the selected subgroup and the next nine); use Inf to print all candidates.

d0.min

Integer. Minimum per-arm filter for candidate subgroups. For "survival" and "binary" outcomes, this is the minimum number of events in the control arm (for binary, events are Y = 1). Ignored for "continuous" outcomes (only n.min applies). Default 10.

d1.min

Integer. Same as d0.min for the treatment arm. Default 10.

max.minutes

Numeric. Currently inert; scheduled for deprecation in v0.3.0. Previously intended as a wall-clock time budget for the combination search, this argument is no longer enforced in the parallelized search path and has no effect on behavior. Search scope is governed by maxk, the candidate-factor front ends (use_grf, use_lasso, conf_force), and the number of parallel workers. The default of 3 is retained only for signature compatibility.

minp

Numeric. Minimum prevalence threshold. Default 0.025.

details

Logical. Print progress details. Default FALSE.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppress the configuration summary message printed at startup. Useful when forestsearch() is called repeatedly inside bootstrap or cross-validation loops. Default FALSE.

maxk

Integer. Maximum number of factors per subgroup. Default 2.

by.risk

Integer. Risk table interval. Default 12.

plot.sg

Logical. Plot subgroup survival curves. Default FALSE.

plot.grf

Logical. Plot GRF results. Default FALSE.

max_subgroups_search

Numeric. Maximum subgroups to evaluate. Default Inf – no truncation. The cap has no counterpart in the method: the candidate family is every conjunction of at most two conditions, less empty intersections and size/event failures, and selection ranges over that family. A finite value truncates the pool under a preview ordering, so the subgroup that is optimal under the actual criterion can be discarded before it is ever evaluated – most acutely for the size foci "maxSG" / "minSG", where small high-effect subgroups sort last, and for the band foci "effMaxSG" / "effMinSG". When a finite value does truncate the pool a warning naming both counts is emitted.

Set a finite value only to bound runtime, knowing it can change which subgroup is selected. The default was 200 in earlier versions.

vi.grf.min

Deprecated (0.4.0.9000): accepted and ignored with a warning. GRF variable-importance screening of the candidate cut columns was removed so that the candidate family is the cut grid alone unless use_lasso, use_grf or use_dina is TRUE. Will be removed in a future release; drop it from the call.

use_twostage

Logical. Use two-stage sequential consistency algorithm for improved performance. Default FALSE for backward compatibility. When TRUE, fs.splits becomes the maximum number of splits, and early stopping is enabled. See Details. Overridden to FALSE under sg_focus = "maxeff" (no two-stage screening).

twostage_args

List. Parameters for two-stage algorithm (only used when use_twostage = TRUE):

n.splits.screen

Integer. Splits for Stage 1 screening. Default 30.

screen.threshold

Numeric. Consistency threshold for Stage 1. Default is automatically calculated to provide ~2.5 SE margin.

batch.size

Integer. Splits per batch in Stage 2. Default 20.

conf.level

Numeric. Confidence level for early stopping. Default 0.95.

min.valid.screen

Integer. Minimum valid Stage 1 splits. Default 10.

consistency_method

Character. "resample" (default) uses the multiplier (influence-function / dfbeta) approximation (consistency_resample), returning the rate from a single subgroup fit; "split" is retained as the fallback and runs the literal repeated 50/50 split-and-refit calculation, which costs fs.splits * 2 refits per candidate evaluation. Despite the name, "resample" performs no numerical resampling at evaluation time – the rate is a closed-form expression. The name reflects the method's derivation: the repeated-split consistency rate admits an equivalent multiplier-resampling (MR) representation, and taking that representation to its analytic limit yields the closed form implemented here. The "resample" path applies to the Cox (survival) outcome and to GLM outcomes whose effect is a single model coefficient (OR, RR, RD, MD, IRR); configurations it cannot represent that way (IRD, propensity-adjusted effects, or a non-convergent fit on a given candidate) fall back to "split" automatically. When use_twostage = TRUE, "resample" bypasses the two-stage split screening entirely (the rate is computed directly).

outcome_type

Character. One of "survival" (default), "binary", "continuous", or "count".

effect_measure

Character or NULL. Effect measure for GLM outcomes. For binary: "OR" (default), "RD", "RR", "IRR", "IRD". For continuous: "MD" (default). For count: "IRR" (default), "IRD". NULL resolves to the per-outcome default shown here; the resolved measure then fixes the scale on which effect.threshold and consistency.threshold are compared – log for the ratio measures ("OR", "RR", "IRR"), identity for "RD", "IRD" and "MD" – so an unset binary call screens on log(1.25) rather than 0.05. See the Threshold vocabulary and resolved defaults section. Ignored for outcome_type = "survival", which always uses the hazard ratio.

offset.name

Character or NULL. Name of the follow-up time column for rate-based measures (IRR, IRD).

adverse_outcome

Logical or NULL. If TRUE, higher outcome values indicate harm (default for binary and count). If FALSE, higher values indicate benefit (default for continuous).

overdispersion

Character. Overdispersion correction for outcome_type = "count". One of "none" (default, standard Poisson), "quasi" (quasi-Poisson), or "negbin" (negative binomial via MASS::glm.nb). Ignored for other outcome types.

grf_count_transform

Character. Transformation applied to the count outcome before passing to grf::causal_forest() for factor screening. "log" (default) applies \(\log(Y + 0.5)\); "identity" passes raw counts. Ignored for non-count outcomes.

tune_grf

Logical. If TRUE, enables cross-validated hyperparameter tuning for GRF's causal_forest() via tune.parameters = "all". If FALSE (default), all GRF parameters remain at their defaults, preserving existing behavior. Applies to both internal GRF pre-screening and standalone GRF analysis when passed through run_simulation_analysis().

adjust_covariates

Character vector or NULL. Additional terms used to adjust the Cox model that scores survival subgroups during consistency evaluation. Terms are appended verbatim to the model right-hand side after the treatment term, so survival modelling helpers may be used directly: adjust_covariates = "strata(x1)" fits a model stratified by x1, whereas adjust_covariates = "x1" includes x1 as a linear covariate. The referenced raw columns must be present in df.analysis; they are carried into the internal scoring frame automatically. Applies to the survival (Cox) consistency path and to GLM outcomes (the effect-estimator closure adds the terms to the outcome model, e.g. logistic for binary/OR). The candidate-search ranking is adjusted on both paths. Mutually exclusive with ps_method != "none". Default NULL (treatment-only, unadjusted – the previous behaviour).

ps_method

Character or NULL. Propensity score estimation method: "grf", "lasso", "logistic", or "none". Default: "none" for RCT, "grf" for observational.

GLM outcome types only ("binary", "continuous", "count"). Propensity adjustment is not implemented for outcome_type = "survival": no Cox estimation path reads the resulting weights, so any value other than "none" is an error there rather than a silent no-op. For confounding control on a survival outcome use adjust_covariates. Note the default resolves to "grf" when is.RCT = FALSE, so an observational survival analysis must pass ps_method = "none" explicitly.

ps_adjust_method

Character. PS adjustment method: "none" (default), "iptw" (stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights), or "dr_gcomp" (IPS covariate).

GLM outcome types only, and consumed only when ps_method is not "none" – it selects how the estimator closure is rebuilt, and that rebuild is GLM-gated. It has no effect on a survival outcome, which is refused at ps_method.

ps_hat

Numeric vector or NULL. User-supplied propensity scores. Must have length equal to nrow(df.analysis), and is applied positionally to df.analysis.

Not carried into bootstrap replicates or cross-validation folds: a resample has the same row count but different subjects, so a supplied score would be attached to the wrong people. Both re-estimate their own score per replicate/fold under ps_method.

mr_inference

Logical. Whether to follow the search with multiplier resampling (MR): a refit-free de-biased estimate of the selected subgroup's treatment effect, an interval for it, and a harm-confirmation flag. Default FALSE, so by default this function performs identification only – no de-biasing, no harm confirmation, and mr_inference / mr_harm_confirmed come back NULL / NA. Setting it TRUE adds a step that runs after the subgroup has been chosen and cannot change that choice. Supported on the GLM resample-consistency path (consistency_method = "resample" with a GLM effect) and on the survival/Cox path (outcome_type = "survival"), where it runs under the default split-consistency search. MR approximates the full bootstrap (forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture) to leading order and does not replace it. See the vocabulary section.

mr_inference_args

List of optional MR controls; used only when mr_inference = TRUE.

confirm_rule

Which harm-confirmation rule to apply to the de-biased estimate: "point" (default) compares the de-biased point estimate to t_confirm; "ci" compares the one-sided 95% selection-adjusted lower bound, and is therefore the stricter requirement.

t_confirm

The threshold confirm_rule compares against, on the effect scale (not the working log scale). NULL (default) resolves to the null effect: 1 for ratio measures, 0 for differences. Set near the null rather than at the screening threshold, because the correction over-shrinks true effects.

reselection

Which selection rule to replay on each perturbed draw when forming the bias term. Defaults to the rule sg_focus implies, so it normally needs no setting.

draws

Number of multiplier draws. Default 2000.

multiplier

Multiplier distribution, default "poisson" (centred Poisson(1) weights, the multiplier-bootstrap analogue of nonparametric-bootstrap multiplicities); also "gaussian", "rademacher".

ci_method

"field" (default) additionally runs the field-calibrated block, whose one-sided bounds are the primary reported products; the de-biased element, its infinitesimal-jackknife SE and its IJ intervals are returned in every call regardless, so nothing is removed – only a per-fit Monte Carlo cost is added. "ij" restores the previous default: the de-biased interval from the infinitesimal-jackknife variance, the leading-order analogue of the full-bootstrap interval, with the field block omitted. "wald" uses the subgroup robust SE and also omits the field block. The naive interval always uses the robust SE.

include_complement

Also de-bias the complement subgroup. Passed as TRUE by every internal caller.

seed

Seed for the multiplier draws; defaults to seedit.

return_reselection

Logical, default FALSE. When TRUE the gate's return gains the reselection element (per-draw winners and the re-selection frequencies p_hat); add-only pass-through, the default reproduces prior output exactly.

field_M_cap

Optional override of the uniform (kappa) sweep's mass-carrying cap; NULL (default) keeps fs_mr_field_uniform()'s default. Consulted only when field_uniform = TRUE.

field_complement

Logical, default FALSE. Under ci_method = "field" with include_complement = TRUE, also evaluate the field block for the complement subgroup, attached as field$complement with the one-sided 95\ bound as its primary product (the benefit-claim orientation; see fs_mr_inference). Add-only pass-through: the default reproduces prior output exactly.

ij_residual

"two_term" (default), "winner" or "winner_floor": which infinitesimal-jackknife residual populates the reported de-biased SE and interval (both blocks); all three SEs are returned side by side regardless (see fs_mr_inference). Add-only pass-through: the default reproduces prior output exactly.

keep_declaration_field, keep_field_matrix

Logical, both default FALSE. Retain the standardized perturbation field that fs_declaration_calibration reads, as mr_inference$declaration_field; keep_field_matrix additionally keeps the full draws-by-candidates matrix (needed for family = "reduced"). Add-only pass-through: unset, nothing is computed or stored and the default reproduces prior output exactly.

declaration_c0

NULL (default) or a numeric vector of pre-specified protected null levels c0 on the natural scale of hr.consistency (c0 <= c2); consulted only with keep_declaration_field = TRUE. The capture then also stores the shifted family maxima Mstar_c0 that fs_declaration_calibration(fit, c0 = ) reads (see fs_mr_inference). Add-only pass-through: unset, nothing is computed or stored.

Value

A list of class "forestsearch" containing:

grp.consistency

Consistency evaluation results including:

  • out_sg: Selected subgroup based on sg_focus

  • sg_focus: Focus criterion used

  • df_flag: Treatment recommendations

  • sg.harm: Subgroup definition labels (character vector of cut names) – same as the top-level sg.harm

  • sg.harm.id: per-subject 0/1 membership indicator (not a character vector of cut expressions; see the Field naming collision section below)

  • algorithm: "twostage" or "fixed"

  • n_candidates_evaluated: Number evaluated

  • n_passed: Number passing threshold

find.grps

Subgroup search results

confounders.candidate

Candidate confounders considered

confounders.evaluated

Confounders after variable selection

df.est

Analysis data with treatment recommendations

df.predict

Prediction data with recommendations (if provided)

df.test

Test data with recommendations (if provided)

minutes_all

Total computation time

grf_res

GRF results object

sg_focus

Subgroup focus criterion used

sg.harm

Selected subgroup definition – character vector of factor-level cut names. Recommended accessor for displaying the identified subgroup (e.g., paste(obj$sg.harm, collapse = " & ")). NULL if no subgroup was identified.

grf_cuts

GRF cut points used

prop_maxk

Proportion of max combinations searched

max_sg_est

Maximum subgroup HR estimate

grf_plot

GRF plot object (if plot.grf = TRUE)

args_call_all

All arguments for reproducibility

threshold_config

The resolved threshold configuration: outcome_type, effect_measure, screening, consistency, screening_natural, consistency_natural, scale, pconsistency and two description strings. Read $scale before reading $screening. The phrase "the screening threshold" names two different numbers depending on which object is inspected:

  • On the survival path $screening is log(hr.threshold) – the scale the admission set and multiplier resampling work on – while the candidate search itself compares the fitted hazard ratio against hr.threshold on the natural scale. The two are the same threshold on two scales, and $screening_natural holds the search's value.

  • On the GLM paths $screening is the value the search compares against directly: the link scale for ratio measures (log of the supplied ratio) and the identity scale for RD, IRD and MD.

$consistency follows the same convention, and $pconsistency is the rate pconsistency.threshold, which has no scale.

family_status

Character scalar recording whether the candidate family the identifier ranked over is fixed – the condition multiplier resampling requires (see mr_inference). "no-front-end": subgroup_method = "consistency" with use_lasso, use_grf and use_dina all FALSE. Named for what it checks: no fitted model shapes the family on the observed data. This is weaker than the manuscript's Section 2.1 fixed family, which additionally requires resample- invariant cut locations – quantile-derived cuts are not. "conditional-removable": the same method with at least one front end on – data-dependent, but fixed by turning those off. "conditional-inherent": subgroup_method of "dina" or "grf", where the family is generated by fitting a model to the same data and cannot be made fixed. Descriptive only; it never raises a condition.

mr_inference

Multiplier-resampling (MR) result, or NULL when MR did not run. See fs_mr_inference for fields (naive, debiased, selection_bias, settings, harm_flag, timing_seconds). MR approximates the full bootstrap (FB) to leading order; its interval is the infinitesimal-jackknife analogue of the FB interval under the default ci_method = "field" and under "ij", and the subgroup robust-SE interval under "wald". Under the default the return also carries the field element.

mr_harm_confirmed

Logical, three-valued. TRUE when MR ran and the de-biased estimate still indicates harm under confirm_rule; FALSE when MR ran and it does not; NA when MR did not run or could not be computed. NA is therefore absence of evidence, not evidence against harm – test it with is.na() before isTRUE(), which collapses NA to FALSE and so reports "harm not confirmed" for an analysis that never ran. See the vocabulary section.

Details

Algorithm Overview:

  1. Variable Selection: GRF identifies variables with treatment effect heterogeneity; LASSO selects most predictive

  2. Subgroup Discovery: Exhaustive search over factor combinations up to maxk

  3. Consistency Validation: Split-sample validation ensures reproducibility

  4. Selection: Choose subgroup based on sg_focus criterion

Two-Stage Consistency Algorithm: When use_twostage = TRUE, the consistency evaluation uses an optimized algorithm that can provide 3-10x speedup:

  • Stage 1: Quick screening with n.splits.screen splits eliminates clearly non-viable candidates

  • Stage 2: Sequential batched evaluation with early stopping for candidates passing Stage 1

The two-stage algorithm is recommended for:

  • Exploratory analyses with many candidate subgroups

  • Large fs.splits values (>200)

  • Iterative model development

For final regulatory submissions, use_twostage = FALSE may be preferred for exact reproducibility.

Threshold vocabulary and resolved defaults

Three arguments carry thresholds, and two of them have the word "consistency" in the name. They are different quantities:

c1 – effect.threshold (legacy hr.threshold)

The screening threshold on a candidate subgroup's own effect, estimated on the full sample. A candidate must clear it to enter the consistency stage.

c2 – consistency.threshold (legacy hr.consistency)

An effect threshold, applied to the subgroup's effect estimated within each split half. Not a proportion, and not the consistency rate.

p* – pconsistency.threshold

A proportion in [0, 1]: the fraction of splits that must clear c2. Not an effect threshold.

In one line: c2 sets the bar a split half must clear, and p* counts how often that bar is met.

Resolved defaults, per estimand. Reading hr.consistency's default as "1.0" is misleading on the GLM paths: when neither threshold is supplied, the value a run actually uses is resolved from the estimand. The resolved pairs are:

resolved estimandc1c2
HR (survival)1.25, compared by the search on the natural HR scale1.0
OR, RR, IRRlog(1.25)log(1.0), i.e. 0
RD0.050.0
IRD0.010.0
MD0.00.0

Supplying effect.threshold or consistency.threshold (or the legacy names) suppresses the corresponding remap and the supplied value is used on the scale shown above.

The pair rule, on the consistency path with a ratio estimand. For subgroup_method = "consistency" with survival (HR) or binary effect_measure = "OR" – the two estimands whose c1 and c2 sit on one comparable ratio scale – the two thresholds are treated as a pair:

  • c2 > c1 is an error. It is degenerate: the consistency-stage entry condition re-screens the admitted family on c2, so candidates the screen let through are discarded at the stage boundary, and when none survives the consistency stage does not run at all and the fit reads as a finding of no subgroup. c2 = c1 is allowed.

  • c1 supplied without c2 derives c2 = 0.80 * c1 on the ratio scale (on the log scale an additive shift of log(0.80), never 0.80 * log(c1)): 1.25 -> 1.00, 1.00 -> 0.80, 0.90 -> 0.72. Announced with a message, and carried into every bootstrap replicate and CV fold. The default pair (1.25, 1.0) is the rule's fixed point, so a call that sets neither threshold is unaffected. An explicitly supplied c2, in either spelling, is never overridden.

  • Supplying both spellings of one threshold at disagreeing values is an error naming both.

Neither rule applies under subgroup_method = "dina" or "grf" (which return before the consistency stage and never consult c2), nor to the identity-scale estimands RD, IRD, MD, nor to IRR.

pconsistency.threshold is not remapped. It is a rate, and it is identical for every outcome_type and every estimand.

Field naming collision with GRF results

The top-level sg.harm on this object and the grp.consistency$sg.harm nested field both hold a character vector of cut expressions. The nested grp.consistency$sg.harm.id field holds a per-subject 0/1 membership indicator, not a cut vector – unlike sg.harm.id on GRF result objects, which does hold cut expressions. See subgroup.consistency and grf.subg.harm.glm for the full discussion of this naming collision. Code that must handle both object types should prefer the top-level sg.harm accessor on forestsearch results.

Vocabulary FB MR and harm confirmation

Four different things in this package used to share the word "gate". They are distinct, they happen at different stages, and only the last one is a pass/fail decision:

Admissibility criteria

Which candidate subgroups are even eligible to be considered: hr.threshold, pconsistency.threshold, n.min, d0.min, d1.min, maxk. Applied during the search.

Selection rule

Which admissible candidate is chosen as the estimated subgroup: sg_focus. Applied during the search.

Post-selection inference

Correcting the chosen subgroup's treatment effect for the optimism of having chosen it, and putting an interval around the corrected value. This is FB and MR below. Applied after the search.

Harm confirmation

The one pass/fail: does the corrected estimate still indicate harm? This is confirm_rule against t_confirm, reported as mr_harm_confirmed.

Full bootstrap (FB) — forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture. Resamples subjects, and re-runs the entire subgroup search inside every replicate, so the replicate may select a different subgroup than the original analysis did. That is what lets it correct the selection-induced bias in the reported treatment effect, and supply an infinitesimal-jackknife interval. It is the reference method, and it is expensive: cost scales with nb_boots times the cost of one search.

Multiplier resampling (MR) — fs_mr_inference, turned on by mr_inference = TRUE. Resamples nothing; it perturbs the per-subject influence contributions (dfbeta) of a single set of fits with random mean-zero multipliers, and re-applies the selection rule on each perturbed draw. It corrects the same selection bias FB corrects and produces the same kind of interval, to leading order, at a small fraction of the cost — no refits. MR is post-selection inference on a completed analysis: it runs after the subgroup has been chosen and cannot change which subgroup is identified. Running with mr_inference = TRUE and FALSE gives identical sg.harm, df.est and max_sg_est. MR approximates FB; it does not replace it.

Harm confirmation. Once MR has produced a de-biased estimate, mr_inference_args$confirm_rule decides whether that estimate still indicates harm:

"point" (default)

Compares the de-biased point estimate to t_confirm.

"ci"

Compares the one-sided 95% selection-adjusted lower bound to t_confirm. Strictly the stronger requirement, so anything it confirms "point" also confirms.

t_confirm is the threshold those rules compare against, on the effect scale (HR, OR, RR, IRR; or RD, MD for differences) — not the working log scale used internally. Left NULL it resolves to the null effect: 1 for ratio measures, 0 for differences. It is deliberately set near the null rather than at hr.threshold, because the de-biasing correction over-shrinks genuine effects, so re-applying the screening threshold to a corrected estimate would discard true findings.

mr_harm_confirmed carries the answer, and is three-valued: TRUE = MR ran and harm is confirmed; FALSE = MR ran and harm is not confirmed; NA = MR did not run, or could not be computed. NA is not evidence against harm. It arises when mr_inference = FALSE (the default), when no subgroup was identified, or when the MR step was skipped or failed for the outcome/consistency combination in use. Because isTRUE(NA) is FALSE, code that reads this field with isTRUE() alone silently reports "harm not confirmed" for an analysis that was never performed; branch on is.na() first.

References

  • FDA Guidance for Industry: Enrichment Strategies for Clinical Trials

  • Athey & Imbens (2016). Recursive partitioning for heterogeneous causal effects. PNAS.

  • Wager & Athey (2018). Estimation and inference of heterogeneous treatment effects using random forests. JASA.

See also

subgroup.consistency for consistency evaluation details forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture for the full bootstrap (FB) fs_mr_inference for multiplier resampling (MR), the mr_inference = TRUE step mr_estimates_table to render the MR estimates fs_fdr_report to sweep harm-confirmation thresholds (c_confirm) and measure what confirmation buys forestsearch_Kfold for cross-validation

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: Standard analysis (backward compatible)
result <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = trial_data,
  sg_focus = "hr",
  hr.threshold = 1.25,
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  fs.splits = 400,
  details = TRUE
)

# Example 2: Fast exploratory analysis with two-stage
result_fast <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = trial_data,
  sg_focus = "maxSG",
  hr.threshold = 1.15,
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.85,
  fs.splits = 500,
  use_twostage = TRUE,
  details = TRUE
)

# Example 3: Two-stage with custom parameters
result_custom <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = trial_data,
  sg_focus = "hr",
  hr.threshold = 1.3,
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.95,
  fs.splits = 600,
  use_twostage = TRUE,
  twostage_args = list(
    n.splits.screen = 50,
    batch.size = 25,
    conf.level = 0.99
  ),
  parallel_args = list(plan = "multisession", workers = 4),
  details = TRUE
)

# Example 4: Binary outcome with OR thresholds
result_binary <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = trial_data,
  outcome_type = "binary",
  effect_measure = "OR",
  effect.threshold = 1.5,
  consistency.threshold = 1.3,
  pconsistency.threshold = 0.90
)

# Example 5: Binary outcome with RD thresholds
result_rd <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = trial_data,
  outcome_type = "binary",
  effect_measure = "RD",
  effect.threshold = 0.07,       # 7 pct-point harm
  consistency.threshold = 0.03   # 3 pct-point per split
)
} # }
